 Follow Deputies Say She Collected $1,223 in Extra SNAP Benefits. Now She Faces Two Felonies
 Milos Komnenovic Mon, November 9, 2026 at 2:45 PM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Image Credit: Cayuga County Sheriff's Office. A New York woman faces two felony charges after investigators said she failed to report income and received $1,223 in excess food assistance. The allegation concerns the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, which helps eligible households purchase food.
 Maria Gonzalez, of Auburn, was arrested October 28 on an outstanding warrant issued by Auburn City Court. Sheriff Brian Schenck described the case in a November 6 announcement reported by FingerLakes1 .
 The Cayuga County Department of Social Services Case Integrity Unit conducted the investigation. The sheriff's Criminal Investigation Division and the District Attorney's Office assisted, according to Finger Lakes Daily News .
 Sheriff's Report Lists Welfare Fraud and Grand Larceny Charges
 The sheriff's November 2 arrest summary records Gonzalez's October 28 arrest and lists fourth-degree welfare fraud and fourth-degree grand larceny. Both are classified as Class E felonies.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Gonzalez was processed at the Public Safety Building and released on an appearance ticket directing her to return to Auburn City Court, according to Finger Lakes Daily News. She is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
 The eCourts case summary identifies the matter as CR-02485-26 and lists an incident date of August 1, 2025. The record, captured November 9, schedules a pretrial conference for December 4 at 9:15 a.m. in Auburn City Court before Judge David B. Thurston.
 Both Charges Carry a Threshold Above $1,000
 A redacted excerpt of the sheriff's November 2 arrest summary lists fourth-degree welfare fraud and fourth-degree grand larceny charges against Maria A. Gonzalez. Document Credit: Cayuga County Sheriff's Office.
 Under New York's fourth-degree welfare fraud law , a fraudulent welfare act that results in more than $1,000 in public assistance benefits can constitute a Class E felony. The grand larceny provision cited in Gonzalez's arrest report also applies to property valued at more than $1,000.
 The alleged $1,223 overpayment exceeds those monetary thresholds, but the amount alone does not establish guilt. New York's definition of a fraudulent welfare act requires knowing conduct and an intent to defraud, along with the other statutory elements.
 SNAP Reporting Rules Depend on the Household
 New York advises recipients that changes in household circumstances may need to be reported depending on the rules applying to their household . Recipients can review the state's SNAP Change Report Form or ask their local social services office which changes and deadlines apply.
 Advertisement Advertisement Changes can be submitted through myBenefits . Cayuga County residents can reach the county SNAP office at 315-253-1210 or visit its third-floor office at 63 Genesee Street in Auburn.
